# Intake Brief: Herdr hydrator — rescue in_progress work items with no active pane

## Headline

Add a hydration task to the herdr worklist plugin that, every 30 seconds, fetches all `in_progress` work items, matches each against the work-item IDs embedded in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace (via the pane-title work WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), and demotes any item with no matching pane out of `in_progress` to `completed` (stage `in_review`), `blocked` (dependency-blocked), or `open` (otherwise). The check also runs immediately when the tab regains focus.

## Problem statement

Work items are sometimes left stuck in `status=in_progress` even though no agent pane is actually working on them (e.g. the agent pane was closed, the session died, or the item was claimed and abandoned). There is currently no automatic mechanism to detect this, so stale in-progress items linger at the top of work queues and are never re-selected.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want a self-healing work queue where an item only stays `in_progress` while an active agent pane is genuinely attached to it.
  - As a producer, I want items whose agent pane has died to be demoted automatically so they re-enter the selection pool instead of rotting in `in_progress`.
- **Herdr worklist users** — benefit from a queue that reflects reality without manual cleanup.
  - As a user, I want the worklist to keep `in_progress` items only when a matching pane exists, so the list stays honest.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every 30 seconds the hydrator fetches all `in_progress` work items (`wl list --status in_progress`).
2. For each item, the hydrator attempts to match an **active pane**: a pane, in **any tab of the current workspace**, whose pane title contains the work item's ID (`WL-…`) and that is still running (present in `herdr pane list`). Matching relies on the pane-title format introduced by the blocking work item (e.g. `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>`).
3. Any `in_progress` item with **no matching active pane** is demoted:
   - stage `in_review` → `status=completed`
   - item has an active outbound dependency blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`) → `status=blocked`
   - otherwise → `status=open`
   Transitions respect the project's status/stage compatibility rules (e.g. `blocked` only allows stages `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`, so a stage `in_progress` item demoted to `blocked` must also have its stage demoted).
4. When the worklist tab regains focus, the hydration check runs **immediately** (not waiting for the next 30s tick), reusing the existing visibility resume-poll mechanism.
5. The hydrator is **safe**: no transition is made for an item whose matching pane is found; the task is single-flight; failures (CLI missing, unparseable output) are logged and never crash the plugin; no `wl` spawns happen while the worklist pane is hidden.
6. Unit tests cover: pane-title ID extraction, active-pane matching across tabs, each demotion decision (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open), stage/status compatibility handling, focus-resume immediate run, and fail-open error paths.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked on WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** ("Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned") — the hydrator matches panes by the work-item ID embedded in pane titles; it must not be implemented before that title format lands. (The in-progress duplicate WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D carries the same work; block on the intake-complete one.)
- The 30s loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker) — acceptable per the operator; the focus-resume immediate check is required.
- "Active pane" = any running pane whose title contains the work-item ID, across **all tabs** in the current workspace; focus/zoom state does not matter (matching is by title presence + pane existence, not focus).
- Reuse the existing `TaskScheduler` (packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts) and the visibility `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery in `worklist.ts`; do not add a second interval loop.
- Fail-open at every boundary: never crash the plugin, never demote on ambiguous evidence (missing pane list, unparseable output → treat as "no match" only when the CLI output is actually trustworthy).
- No schema changes; pure status/stage updates via the `wl` CLI.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the worklist TUI registers a single `TaskScheduler` with tasks: `refresh` (auto-refresh), `sync`, `resume-poll` (hidden→visible immediate refresh), and `downtime` (downtime-worker tick, 30s default). The hydrator would be a sibling task.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — `TaskScheduler` with 1s base tick, per-task `intervalMs`, `singleFlight`, and `runTimeoutMs` watchdog; a rejecting task never takes down the loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — `isPaneVisible()` + `PollGate` (TTL memoizer); tab focus via `herdr tab get <id>` is the visibility signal; resume-poll uses it to detect hidden→visible.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — existing work-item ↔ pane association file (`.worklog/agent-panes.json`) and `herdr agent list` parsing; a possible secondary signal but the hydrator matches by pane-title per the operator's decision.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `runWl(...)`, `extractJson`, `extractItems` helpers for wl CLI JSON.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/toggle.sh` — precedent for `herdr pane list` JSON parsing (panes with `label`/`pane_id` across the workspace).
- `src/commands/dep.ts` — `wl dep list <id>` returns `outbound` edges with target `id`/`status`/`priority`; `packages/shared/src/database.ts:isDependencyActive` defines an active blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`).
- `src/config.ts` — status/stage compatibility: `in-progress` allows `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`; `blocked` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`; `completed` allows `in_review`/`done`; `open` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`.

## Desired change

1. Add a hydrator module (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`):
   - `extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes)` — parse `WL-[0-9A-Z]+` from pane titles.
   - `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes)` — item ID present in any running pane title across all tabs.
   - `decideDemotion(item)` — pure decision: `in_review` → `completed`; dependency-blocked → `blocked`; else → `open` (with stage/status compatibility handling).
   - `runHydrationOnce(deps)` — fetch `wl list --status in_progress`, fetch `herdr pane list`, match, apply demotions via `wl update`.
2. Register the hydrator in `worklist.ts` as a scheduler task (`id: 'hydrate'`, `intervalMs: 30_000`, `singleFlight: true`, `runTimeoutMs` set) that is visibility-gated (skip while hidden, zero wl spawns when hidden).
3. Hook the hidden→visible transition: when the resume-poll detects visibility, run the hydration check immediately in addition to the existing refresh.
4. Add unit tests (see AC6) mirroring the existing downtime-worker test harness (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, injectable exec seam from `fetcher.ts`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — new module: ID extraction, pane matching, demotion decision, orchestration (the bulk of the work).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — register the `hydrate` scheduler task; trigger immediate check on focus-resume.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — reused as-is (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — reused `runWl`/`extractJson`/`extractItems` helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — reused `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — new test suite (AC6).
- `src/config.ts` — reference only: status/stage compatibility rules that constrain demotion.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — reference only: dependency-blocked semantics (`isDependencyActive`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** — "Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned" (open, intake_complete) — **BLOCKING**: introduces the pane-title format containing the work-item ID that the hydrator matches on. In-progress duplicate: **WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D** (same title).
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — "Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon" (in_review) — pane↔work-item association machinery; `agent-panes.json` is a candidate secondary signal.
- **WL-0MS9NPHQU005Y3VE** — "Herdr plugin should set work-item status to in_progress when instigating actions" (completed) — the counter-direction: sets `in_progress` on dispatch; the hydrator demotes when no pane remains.
- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (completed) — downtime worker: the 30s scheduler-task precedent the hydrator mirrors.
- **WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35** — "Gate worklist auto-refresh on tab focus so a visible pane in a multi-pane tab keeps refreshing" (in_progress) — visibility-gating precedent reused by the hydrator.
- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — "Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible" (completed) — related zero-spawn-when-hidden concern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** pane titles will contain the work-item ID once WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y lands — the hydrator is blocked on that and must not guess other signals.
- **Risk:** demoting an item the operator considers genuinely in-progress (pane title missing/renamed by hand, pane in a different workspace). Mitigation: matching is by title + pane existence across all tabs; the 30s cadence + focus-resume means demotions are re-visible quickly; keep the demotion decision pure and well-tested.
- **Risk:** status/stage compatibility rejects a demotion (e.g. `blocked` with stage `in_progress`). Mitigation: `decideDemotion` returns a compatible (status, stage) pair; transitions that fail validation are logged, not retried blindly.
- **Risk:** `herdr pane list` output shape differs (tabs vs panes). Mitigation: fail-open parsing like toggle.sh/agent-tracker; treat unparseable output as "no demotion this cycle".
- **Risk:** scope creep (agent-panes.json matching, notifications, configurable intervals). Mitigation: record as linked work items; this intake covers pane-title matching only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** secondary signals (agent-panes.json, `herdr agent list` states) are explicitly out of scope for the initial implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When no active pane matches an in_progress item, HOW should the hydrator choose between completed / blocked / open? (a) Signal-based: stage in_review → completed; blocked-by dependencies → blocked; otherwise → open; (b) always open; (c) operator picks per item; (d) other" — Answer (user): **a** — signal-based. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "The herdr plugin's 30s scheduler loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker). That means the hydrator only runs while a worklist pane is open. Acceptable, or should it run standalone?" — Answer (user): **acceptable**, ensure the check runs immediately when the tab gets focus. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Does 'active pane' mean any pane whose title contains the work-item ID and is still running (regardless of focus/zoom), across all tabs in the current workspace?" — Answer (user): **yes**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** – Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon (completed)

# Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J)

## Headline

Flip the space priority in the Herdr worklist pane: the selection list may use up to the full available pane height (including its header lines), and the metadata section fills whatever space remains — expanding when the list is short, sitting below the fold (revealed by scrolling down) when the list is long — scrolling internally when its content overflows.

## Problem statement

The metadata section below the selection list currently reserves a fixed 20–40% of the pane height (`computeMetadataPanelHeight`), squeezing the list. When the list needs more vertical space than it is allotted, it scrolls and the header/top lines scroll off the top of the pane, even though the metadata section below is eating rows the list could use. The metadata section should no longer force the list to scroll off the top.

## Users

- **Herdr users (human and AI agent)** browsing the work item list in a pane, who want the selection list — including its header line — to use as much vertical space as it needs, up to the maximum available, so items don't scroll off the top prematurely.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, when the list is long, I want the list (header + items) to take up to the full pane height so I can see as many items as possible without the top scrolling off.
- As a Herdr user, when the list is short, I want the metadata section to expand into the leftover space so the pane still shows the selected item's metadata.
- As a Herdr user, when the list fills the full pane, I want to scroll the pane down to expose the rest of the list and then the metadata section, with the initial view starting at the top of the selection list.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **List takes as much space as it needs, up to the max available**: The selection list (header line + items + group separators + footer) can use up to the maximum number of vertical lines available in the pane (pane rows minus the reserved notification row). The metadata section no longer reserves a fixed 20–40% share that forces the list to scroll.
2. **Initial view at top**: When the list fills the full vertical space, the view starts at the top of the selection list (header + first items visible). Scrolling the pane down exposes the rest of the list and, at the end, the metadata section.
3. **Metadata fills the rest**: When the list content is shorter than the available height, the metadata section expands to fill the leftover space below the list.
4. **Metadata scrolls if necessary**: When the metadata content overflows the space allotted to it, it scrolls independently using the existing `m`/`M` keys and `metaScrollOffset` (with the existing `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator), and the selection-driven reset behaviour is preserved.
5. **No regression**: Keyboard navigation (arrows/j/k, PgUp/PgDn, g/G, wrap), stage filtering, group separators, auto-refresh, code-freeze banner, and the reserved notification row continue to work; rendered output never exceeds the pane's `rows` budget.
6. **Testing**: Unit tests cover (a) list height = min(content need, max available), (b) metadata expansion when the list is short, (c) reveal-by-scroll when the list fills the pane and initial view at top, (d) metadata scroll clamping under the new layout, and (e) the output line-count invariant (≤ `rows`).
7. **Docs**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** — managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Plugin-local change in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; no `wl` CLI or backend schema changes.
- The rendered output must never exceed the pane's `rows` budget (last row reserved for the notification line; group-separator accounting must not overflow) — the invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO must hold.
- Preserve existing keyboard bindings: `m`/`M` for metadata scrolling, and all list-navigation keys unchanged.
- Must compose with the description preview feature (WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3, in progress) which adds up to 3 preview lines to the metadata panel content.
- The metadata panel keeps a small minimum height (~3 rows) whenever it is rendered (short list or scrolled into view) so it remains usable, even if that means its content scrolls internally.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — document-flow layout**: the user's answers describe the list and metadata section as stacked content within one scrollable viewport (view starts at top; scrolling down reveals the rest of the list, then the metadata). An alternative pinned-footer layout (metadata always visible at the pane bottom) does not match the answers and is out of scope.
- **Assumption — header behavior**: "start the view at the top of the selection list" is interpreted as the initial render showing header + first items; the exact pin-vs-scroll behaviour of the header line during scroll is an implementation detail, but the header must be visible initially (matching the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO invariant that the header is never cut off).
- **Risk — line-count regression**: changing the list/metadata space split could reintroduce output overflowing the pane (the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO bug). Mitigation: keep the ≤ `rows` invariant as an explicit test.
- **Risk — metadata scroll clamping**: if the panel's allotted height changes dynamically, `metaScrollDown`'s clamp against content height must still hold; keep the existing clamp tests and update them for the new sizing.
- **Risk — scope creep**: "below the fold" indicators (WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ), mouse/touch scrolling (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ), and metadata panel content changes (WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7) are related but separate items — do not implement them here.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:
  - `computeMetadataPanelHeight(rows)` (lines ~85–119) — reserves a 20–40% share of pane rows for the metadata panel (min 3 rows), from WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X.
  - `WorkItemListState._listHeight()` (line ~681) — `max(3, rows - 4 - panelHeight)`; used by `_adjustScroll` and `getVisibleItems`.
  - `createListRenderer()` (line ~1830) — computes `panelHeight = computeMetadataPanelHeight(rows)`, `listArea = rows - 1 - panelHeight`, `listHeight = rows - 4 - panelHeight`; renders header + items + separators + fill + footer + metadata panel lines, clamped to `rows - 1`.
  - `formatMetadataPanel()` (line ~982) — renders exactly `panelRows` lines with independent scroll offset and `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator; `metaScrollDown` clamps against content height.
  - `metaScrollOffset` reset on selection change (`_resetMetaScroll`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `computeMetadataPanelHeight` responsive-ramp tests (lines ~1448), metadata scroll clamp tests (line ~1663), renderer line-count invariant tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — entry point wiring (render callback passes `metaScrollOffset`/`metaLastCommand`).

## Desired change

- In `createListRenderer()`: compute the list's space need from its content (header + banner + items + separators + footer), capped at the maximum available rows (`rows - 1` minus the notification budget). The metadata section is allotted the remainder: it expands to fill leftover space when the list is short, and when the list fills the pane it is positioned below the list content so scrolling down reveals the rest of the list and then the metadata section.
- Initial view starts at the top of the selection list (scroll offset 0 / header visible) even when the list is long.
- Keep `computeMetadataPanelHeight` (or replace its call sites) such that the fixed 20–40% reservation no longer forces the list to scroll; the metadata panel keeps a small minimum height (~3 rows) and scrolls internally via `metaScrollOffset`/`m`/`M` when its content overflows.
- Keep `formatMetadataPanel`'s independent-scroll contract (exactly `panelRows` lines) and the `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — list/metadata space split, initial view-at-top, metadata scroll clamping; primary change location.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — update responsive-ramp tests; add list-height/content-need, metadata-expansion, reveal-by-scroll, and line-count invariant tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — render callback wiring (`metaScrollOffset`, `metaLastCommand`), only if the space split needs state/context passed through.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** (completed) — introduced the metadata panel and the fixed 20–40% reservation this item reverses; its AC1 said the list "always keeps the majority of the space (≥60%)" — this item changes that priority.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** (in progress) — adds a description preview to the metadata panel (up to 3 lines), which makes the metadata content taller; this item must compose with it.
- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO** (completed) — the output line-count invariant (`≤ rows`) this item must preserve.
- **WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ** (open) — "no indication of items below the fold" — related scrolling UX; not required by this item but related.
- **WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7** (open) — drops the duplicate ID row from the metadata panel; touches the same `formatMetadataPanel` output.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When the list is long and fills the pane, should the metadata panel keep a small guaranteed minimum (e.g., ~3 rows, as today) so it stays visible and scrolls within that, or may it shrink all the way to zero (hidden)?" — Answer (user): "If the selection list takes up the full vertical space scrolling the pane down should expose the rest of the list and the meta-data section. However we should start the view at the top of the selection list." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: when the list fills the pane, the metadata section sits below the list content and is revealed by scrolling the pane down; the initial view starts at the top of the selection list (header visible). Research: inspected `computeMetadataPanelHeight` (20–40% fixed reservation) and the renderer's `listArea`/`listHeight` budget in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Q2: "When the list has only a few items, should the list take only the rows it needs (header + items + separators + footer) and let the metadata panel expand to fill the leftover space, or should the list always occupy the full available height and the metadata panel stay at a fixed small size?" — Answer (user): "meta-data can expand to fill space." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: the list takes only what it needs when short; the metadata section expands into the leftover space.
- Q3: "Should the existing m/M metadata scrolling behavior stay as-is, just operating in the new (possibly smaller) panel space?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. Research: `metaScrollOffset`, `_resetMetaScroll` on selection change, `metaScrollUp/Down` clamping and the `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator already exist in `worklist.ts`.

## Problem statement

During the 2026-08-20 system hang, \"Under memory pressure, flushing caches\" appeared 10+ times in the journal between 13:27 and 13:40 with no alert and no early warning. The system ran for 21 days with accumulating memory pressure and no monitoring to catch it before it became unusable.

## Goal

Install lightweight memory-pressure monitoring so a repeat of the 2026-08-20 memory exhaustion is detected and alerted on well before the system becomes unresponsive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A monitoring mechanism is installed (e.g. cron/systemd timer script checking /proc/meminfo MemAvailable, or earlyoom/PSI-based monitoring via /proc/pressure/memory)
- [ ] An alert fires when MemAvailable drops below a threshold (e.g. 2 GB) - alert method documented (logger/journald entry, desktop notification, or both)
- [ ] Historical trend is captured so memory exhaustion can be diagnosed after the fact (e.g. collectd/sysstat already captures sar data - verify and document retention)
- [ ] The alert mechanism is tested end-to-end once (verified alert emission)
- [ ] Setup and thresholds documented in a comment on this work item or docs

## Suggested approach

```bash
# /etc/cron.d/memwatch (example)
* * * * * root [ $(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo) -lt 2048 ] && logger -p user.warning "LOW MEMORY: $(awk '/MemAvailable/ {printf \"%.0fMB
\", $2/1024}' /proc/meminfo)"
```

Consider also monitoring /proc/pressure/memory (PSI) for sustained pressure events, which is what journald's \"Under memory pressure\" messages derive from.

## Key files

- /proc/meminfo, /proc/pressure/memory, /var/log/sysstat (sar data if installed)

# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`
- Non-terminal transitions (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must NOT change priority

### Key Files
- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — helper function location
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — priority constants
data.title: Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, when the local LLM is idle, I want the herdr downtime
worker to avoid starting **non-critical** implementations while the
completed/in_review review queue is already deep enough to fill the
selection list, so the producer-review bottleneck is not overloaded.
Auditing, intake, and planning can still be dispatched — only the
implement tier is gated.

## Background

- Dispatch tier order (dispatchDowntimeWork): scheduled prompts → audit →
  implement → plan → intake. The code-freeze gate (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY)
  already skips audit+implement during a release; this is a second,
  orthogonal implement-tier-only throttle on the producer-review queue.
- The herdr selection list displays up to `browseItemCount` items
  (default 20, clamp 1–50, packages/herdr/src/settings.ts).
- Review-queue count = completed/in_review **root** items
  (`wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json`) —
  same query family as the audit tier (WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG) and the
  selection list's mandatory review subset (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
  Operator decision (2026-08): count is ROOT-ONLY, not all items.
- Implement candidates carry `priority` (critical/high/medium/low) via
  parseImplementCandidatesOutput.

## Design notes

- Gate: when `reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount`, the implement tier
  selects only candidates with `priority === 'critical'`; non-critical
  candidates are excluded and dispatch falls through to plan/intake.
- Critical priority BYPASSES the gate — a critical implement always stays
  eligible regardless of queue depth.
- Fail-closed: a wl error counting the review queue → gate active (only
  critical implements), consistent with the code-freeze "ambiguous ⇒
  frozen" convention.
- `browseItemCount` is re-read live from settings on each dispatch (no
  plugin restart needed), matching the existing config() re-read pattern.
- The gate skip must NOT look like an empty backlog: when implement
  candidates exist but are gated AND plan/intake are empty, the outcome
  must be a neutral reason (never 'no-candidate'), so the worker's
  no-candidate cooldown is not triggered — polling continues and a
  critical implement / new plan / intake item dispatches immediately
  (mirrors the code-freeze 'code-freeze' reason convention).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A critical-priority implement candidate is always eligible regardless
   of review-queue depth (critical bypasses the gate).
2. When reviewQueueCount < browseItemCount, implement-tier selection is
   UNCHANGED: all priorities eligible; risk/effort/dispatched-marker
   filters unchanged.
3. When reviewQueueCount >= browseItemCount, non-critical implement
   candidates are excluded; if only non-critical candidates remain,
   getNextImplementCandidate resolves null and dispatch falls through to
   plan/intake (no-candidate only when plan AND intake are genuinely
   empty; a gate skip with an empty plan/intake backlog is a neutral
   reason, never 'no-candidate').
4. The gate applies ONLY to the implement tier — audit, plan, intake,
   and scheduled-prompt dispatch are unaffected.
5. The review-queue count query is bounded by DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS and
   fail-closed (error ⇒ gate active).
6. Tests cover: gate boundary (count == listSize − 1 vs count == listSize),
   critical bypass, root-only counting, fall-through outcome, and the
   neutral (no-cooldown) reason on a gate skip with empty plan/intake.

## Related work

- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — Implement tier end-to-end in herdr downtime worker
- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — Audit tier (completed/in_review without valid audit)
- WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY — Code-freeze gate
- WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B — Selection list must always show all
  completed/in_review and critical items
data.title: Downtime dispatch: gate non-critical implement tier on review-queue depth

data.description:
As an operator, I do not want a transient failure in the downtime dispatch pipeline to strand a work item in `in_progress` with no agent working it and no automatic recovery.

## Background

- dispatchClaimedTier (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts) pipeline: CAS claim → marker write → spawn.
- Gap 1 from the dispatch decision-point evaluation: if the marker write fails (D16) AFTER the CAS claim succeeds, the outcome is reason 'marker-write-failed' and the item stays `in_progress` — but the claim is never rolled back. The item is then invisible to every later tier: plan/implement tiers select `status === 'open'`, the audit tier selects `completed`. Only manual intervention recovers it.
- Same class of issue on 'spawn-failed' (D17): the marker stands (kind `implement`/`plan`/`audit` at the dispatched-at stage), so even after a human reverts the item to `open`, the dispatched-marker exclusion keeps it out of selection until the stage changes — a transient send-to-pi.sh failure (e.g. ENOENT) permanently removes a never-worked item from the idle-slot queue.
- Existing design intent (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 2): "an unmarked item is never dispatched" — this is sound; the gap is the missing RECOVERY path, not the fail-closed abort.

## Design notes

- Option A (rollback): on 'marker-write-failed', restore the item to its pre-claim state (CAS reverse: `wl update <id> --status open --if-status in_progress [--if-stage ...]`) so the next idle period can select it again.
- Option B (requeue for spawn-failed): on 'spawn-failed', write a distinct marker variant (e.g. `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries are already appended) and have the marker-exclusion readers treat a spawn-failed marker as NON-excluding (item is re-eligible) while still logging the failure — the rolling log already distinguishes attempted vs opened (WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U AC2).
- Both options preserve the fail-closed invariant (a marker-less item is never dispatched twice concurrently); the CAS claim already serializes re-selection.
- Decide and document whether the re-dispatch window should be immediate (next idle) or after a short backoff to avoid spawn-failure hot loops.

## Acceptance criteria

# Active-audit detection & audit-tier skip

## Summary

Add an active-audit detection dependency (`getActiveAudit(cwd)`) that reads `kind=audit` dispatch markers from `downtime-dispatches.log` within a 2-hour stale window and confirms the item is still `in_progress` via a single worklog query; gate the audit tier in `dispatchDowntimeWork` and log the skip reason `audit-in-flight`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit sequential enforcement** — Before dispatching an audit-tier item, the dispatcher checks whether any audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (dispatched but not yet completed/reviewed). If one exists, the audit tier is skipped and the dispatcher falls through to the next tier.
2. **Check mechanism** — The dispatcher queries the worklog for audit-tier items that have a corresponding dispatch entry in `downtime-dispatches.log` with `kind` `audit`; a dispatched audit entry older than a stale threshold (2 hours) is treated as stale and ignored (audit pane may have crashed without updating the work item).
3. **Stale window constant** — A named constant `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_STALE_WINDOW_MS` (= 2 hours) defines the stale threshold; entries older than it are ignored.
4. **Active audit blocks new dispatch** — If an active (non-stale) audit is found, the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to the implement tier; the skip reason `audit-in-flight` is logged for observability, and when the remaining backlog is empty the outcome is `audit-in-flight` (never `no-candidate`), so the no-candidate cooldown is not entered (mirrors `code-freeze`).
5. **Fail-open on check failure** — If the active-audit check cannot complete (e.g., worklog query fails), the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to the implement tier; dispatch is never blocked.
6. **Existing guards preserved** — The single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`), CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion, and code-freeze gate continue to work unchanged.
7. **Leader-only check scope** — Only the elected leader performs the active-audit check; the check is placed in the audit-tier dispatch path only (leader-only under WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL), with no new instance-local state, so non-leader instances do not dispatch audits (unchanged behavior).

# Dispatched audits: use both cheap slots during Phase 2 deep analysis

## Problem statement

The downtime worker pins `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` for dispatched audits (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS) so an audit's Phase 2 child deep-analysis runs strictly sequentially (parent first, then one child at a time). This guarantees one audit fits cheap mode's 2-slots (parent + 1 child = 2) — but it also means a single dispatched audit NEVER uses more than one slot at a time during almost its entire run: Phase 1 is a single stream, and Phase 2 children serialize.

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap window (2026-08-22) shows the local model busy only ~25-38% while these audits ran — the second slot sat idle. The audit chain ran 17 child sessions with ~12s gaps, then multi-minute gaps between dispatched runs.

Raising the fan-out to 2 would let one child run concurrently with the parent (2 slots busy) during deep analysis — but the current bound (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS) exists precisely to keep child-heavy audits inside the cheap 2-slot pool. Parent + 2 children = 3 concurrent streams would fall back to remote. This item must therefore be coordinated with the concurrent-dispatch item so the combined in-flight stream budget never exceeds cheap capacity (2 slots).

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants higher overnight local utilization without pushing more traffic to fallback (429-capped) remotes.
- **Herdr downtime users** — want child-heavy audits to complete faster.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Phase 2 deep-analysis concurrency for dispatched audits is mode-aware: 1 (current serial behavior) in fast mode or whenever the combined dispatch budget would exceed the cheap 2-slot pool; 2 when a second slot is genuinely free (coordinated with the concurrent-dispatch item).
2. Parent + N children as a single audit run never produces more concurrent local streams than the cheap-mode slot budget (2 in cheap mode).
3. No audit-skill changes (agent-infrastructure boundary — the skill already honours the env var); change lives in `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`).
4. Tests: env var value is mode/budget-dependent; spawn options for cheap mode with a free second slot include `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM: '2'`; fast mode or full pool keeps `'1'`.
5. Measured outcome: dispatched audit Phase 2 wall-clock drops (children overlap the parent) and/or cheap-window busy % rises vs. the 25-38% baseline, without increasing remote fallback rate.

## Notes

- History: WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (completed) set `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` with rationale "cheap mode = 2 slots = parent + 1 child" — the audit skill default is 2, which the bound overrode to prevent 3-stream fallback. This item revisits that bound for the slot-idle case rather than reverting it.
- Default `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` handling lives in `audit_runner.py` (`AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM_ENV` / legacy alias) — pinned env in the pane spawn wins over the skill default.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (fan-out bound), plus the proxy usage report's recommendation #3.

# Faster downtime dispatch cadence: reduce poll interval and idle threshold

## Problem statement

The downtime worker polls the proxy status every `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (default 10s, hard floor `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS` = 10s) and requires the model to be continuously idle for `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (default 60s, floor 1s) before dispatching. Per dispatch cycle this imposes ~70s of scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn/claim overhead).

During the 04:00-06:00 cheap window (2026-08-22 proxy usage analysis) inter-run gaps of 141s, 146s and 312s were observed between consecutive dispatched runs — a large fraction (est. ~13% of the window) attributable to this threshold+poll+spawn cadence, on top of the model being idle ~50-68% of the time. The current 10s poll floor is a hard-coded guard ("must not hammer the proxy") rather than a measured load limit; the 60s idle threshold is a conservative default from the early worker design.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants more work dispatched into the idle overnight windows; lower latency between dispatch opportunities.
- **Herdr downtime users** — more items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both knobs stay configurable via downtime settings (existing `pollIntervalMs` / `idleThresholdMs` pattern) with **lowered floors**:
   - poll interval floor reduced from 10s to a measured-safe value (target 5s; assert proxy `/llama/local/status` call volume stays negligible — status endpoint is cheap and local);
   - idle threshold floor reduced to ≥1s (current floor) but adjusted production default lowered from 60s to a tuned value (target 15-30s) for the cheap window.
2. Defaults: cheap/downtime mode adopts the faster cadence; interactive or operator-session-sensitive paths unchanged.
3. The idle-gate semantics are preserved: dispatch still only occurs after the model has been continuously idle for the (shorter) threshold — no dispatch into a busy slot, no claim race with the existing single-flight safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
4. Tests updated: floor enforcement (values below floor rejected/clamped), cadence honored in the poll loop, idle-gate still requires the threshold to elapse, no dispatch while slots busy.
5. Measured outcome: mean inter-dispatch gap in the cheap window drops vs. baseline (146s/312s observed), and/or more sessions dispatched per night, without breaching proxy status-endpoint load limits.

## Notes

- Constants in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`: `DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_FLOOR_MS = 10_000`, `DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_FLOOR_MS = 1_000`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000`, `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 60_000`.
- The 10s floor comment says "must not hammer the proxy" — quantify actual load before lowering; the status endpoint (`/llama/local/status`) is a cheap local JSON read, so the floor is expected to be safely reducible.
- Recommended: couple with the concurrent-dispatch item (bounded concurrency) so the faster cadence feeds more than one slot rather than just firing more single dispatches.
- Related: WL-0MSG80254005ZNE9 (proxy status poller), WL-0MSG80J5W007DVJ4 (timer loop), WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (idle tracker); evidence in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`.

## Goal
Implement the regression detection layer on top of the existing merge logic in `mergeSameTimestampItems` and `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`. The guard must detect when a field regresses from non-default → default in newer remote state and report/refuse it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Regression detection identifies fields regressing from non-default → default in merge-participating fields: `status`, `stage`, `priority`, `assignee`.
2. When a regression is detected, it is recorded in the conflict report with full details (item id, field, old local value, new remote default value).
3. The regression is **refused** — the local non-default value is kept and the remote default is NOT imported.
4. The existing non-default-preference behavior (`!localIsDefault && remoteIsDefault` branch) is preserved for non-regression cases — this guard must NOT change legitimate conflict resolution where both sides changed from defaults to different non-default values.
5. effort/risk regressions are reported as protected conflicts (local kept) but these fields remain excluded from the merge lists entirely.
6. Both same-timestamp and different-timestamp merge paths include the detection.
7. Close state preservation (status=completed + terminal stage) is NOT affected — it continues to work as before.

## Implementation Notes

The existing merge logic in `mergeSameTimestampItems` and `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` already has the `!localIsDefault && remoteIsDefault` branch that silently keeps the local value. The regression guard adds a detection/reporting layer on top:

- Before the silent-keep, check if the remote value is a regression (non-default → default transition from the local perspective).
- A "regression" is specifically: local has a non-default value AND remote sends its default (meaning the remote has "lost" the value).
- Record this as a conflict detail with the new conflict type `regression`.
- When `acceptRegressions` option is false (default), refuse the import; when true, allow the import.

**Merge field arrays (UNCHANGED):**
`[title, description, status, priority, sortIndex, parentId, tags, assignee, stage, issueType, createdBy, deletedBy, deleteReason]`

**Regression target fields (subset):**
`[status, stage, priority, assignee]`

**Protected (excluded) fields:**
`effort`, `risk` — never in merge lists; regressions reported as protected.

## Key Files
- `src/sync.ts` — `mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`: add regression detection
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — `isDefaultValue`: may need no changes
- `src/types.ts` — add `regression` conflict type to `ConflictDetail` union if not present

## Problem

When hovering the mouse cursor over a work-item row in the Herdr worklist that has an associated agent-pane, the user has no quick way to see the work-item metadata. The metadata panel at the bottom only shows info for the **selected** row.

## Solution

Add a hover tooltip overlay in the footer area that shows essential work-item metadata for any row the mouse hovers over, when that row has an associated agent-pane. Pressing `Esc` closes the tooltip until the mouse exits and re-enters the pane boundaries.

### Displayed Metadata

For a work item with an associated agent-pane, the tooltip shows:

| Field | Source |
|---|---|
| ID | `workItem.id` |
| Title | `workItem.title` |
| Command | Stored command dispatched to the pane (e.g. `/skill:implement WL-123`) |
| Priority | `workItem.priority` |
| Type | `workItem.issueType` |
| Risk | `workItem.risk` |
| Effort | `workItem.effort` |
| Start Time | `AgentPaneEntry.recordedAt` (ISO timestamp) |

### Data Model Changes

Currently, `AgentPaneEntry` in `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` stores only `workItemId`, `paneId`, and `recordedAt`. The **command** field must be added:

```typescript
interface AgentPaneEntry {
  workItemId: string;
  paneId: string;
  recordedAt: string;
  /** The command dispatched to this pane (e.g. "/skill:implement WL-123"). */
  command?: string;
}
```

### Mouse Hover Handling

The worklist already has SGR mouse tracking (`consumeMouseChunk`, `mapMouseToAction`). Currently, motion events (button & 32) return `null` and are inert. The tooltip feature extends this:

- Track mouse motion events to determine which row the cursor is over
- Map the y-coordinate to a row index via `mapListRowToIndex`
- Look up the work item in `items` at that index
- Check if the work item has an associated pane via `agentTracker.getPaneId(workItemId)`
- If yes, render the tooltip overlay in the footer area
- Pressing `Esc` dismisses the tooltip; it reappears on next mouse enter into the list area

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hover tooltip renders** — When the mouse cursor is over a work-item row with an associated agent-pane, a tooltip appears showing all 8 metadata fields above (ID, Title, Command, Priority, Type, Risk, Effort, Start Time).
2. **Esc dismisses** — Pressing `Esc` closes the tooltip immediately. The tooltip reappears the next time the mouse re-enters the list area over a pane-associated row.

4. **Command stored** — The command string (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`) is persisted in the `agent-panes.json` state file when recording the pane association.
5. **No regression** — Existing mouse interactions (click, double-click, wheel navigation) continue to work correctly. Motion events that would trigger the tooltip are consumed and do not leak to keyboard handlers.
5. **Data migration** — The `agent-panes.json` reader handles entries that lack the new `command` field (backward compatible).
6. **Tests** — Unit tests cover: tooltip state machine (show/dismiss/re-show), motion-to-row mapping, metadata formatting, backward-compatible `agent-panes.json` parsing.

# Use markdown rendering in description preview (metadata panel)

## Problem statement

The description preview in the metadata panel shows raw markdown source lines
(up to 3 non-empty lines), with no formatting — headings, bold, links, code,
and lists all render as literal text. The detail view already uses
`renderMarkdown()` for the same content with full styling. Users expect the
preview to convey the same visual information as the detail view.

## Users

- **Herdr operators** browsing the selection list want to quickly gauge what a
  work item is about without opening the detail view. A properly formatted
  preview (with headings, bold, links) communicates meaning much faster than
  raw text.

- **Producers** reviewing items in the list mode need to see structured content
  (e.g., a bolded summary line, a link to a design doc) at a glance.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Markdown rendering** — `buildDescriptionPreview()` is replaced with a
   function that calls `renderMarkdown()` (from `md-viewer.ts`) on the item's
   description, producing styled terminal lines instead of raw source lines.
2. **Available-space layout** — The preview fills available panel space: the
   selection list takes precedence (dynamic layout), the metadata panel fills
   the remainder, and the description preview consumes the full panel height
   (respecting the 3-row minimum only when other metadata lines are present).
3. **Cached rendering** — Rendered output is cached per item (keyed by item ID
   + description hash) so the markdown parser runs only once per selection
   change; on refresh of the same item, the cached output is reused. Cache
   invalidation occurs on item refresh, selection change, and when the
   description is modified externally.
4. **Construct parity** — Headings (h1–h6), bold, italic, strikethrough, links,
   inline code, fenced code blocks, blockquotes, lists (ordered and nested),
   tables, and horizontal rules all render correctly via `renderMarkdown()`.
5. **ANSI safety** — Rendered lines are properly truncated to panel width; ANSI
   sequences are not broken by truncation. No line exceeds the terminal width.
6. **Tests updated** — Existing `formatMetadataPanel` description preview tests
   are updated to cover markdown rendering; new tests verify cache behavior,
   line width safety, and construct rendering.
7. **Backward compatibility** — No visible change to items without descriptions;
   the preview section is omitted when description is missing/blank (unchanged).

## Constraints

- Performance: markdown rendering must not cause frame drops. Caching is
  mandatory.
- The selection list must always retain layout priority — the metadata panel
  never steals rows from the list.
- The metadata panel's minimum height (3 rows) is preserved when there is no
  description.

## Existing state

- `buildDescriptionPreview()` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` splits the
  description by `
`, takes up to 3 non-empty lines, and renders them with
  simple padding and truncation.
- `renderMarkdown()` in `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts` is a mature, fully
  tested renderer used in the detail view.
- The metadata panel already supports scrolling via `metaScrollOffset`.
- Dynamic layout (`computeDynamicLayout`) ensures the selection list takes
  priority.

## Desired change

Replace `buildDescriptionPreview` with a markdown-aware preview function that:
1. Calls `renderMarkdown()` to produce styled terminal lines
2. Limits output to available panel space
3. Caches results keyed by (item.id, descriptionHash)
4. Integrates cleanly with existing `formatMetadataPanel` scrolling

## Related work

- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** — Initial description preview (completed, raw lines)
- **`md-viewer.ts`** — Full markdown renderer used in detail view (already
  tested, no changes needed)
- **WL-0MSKFFJWD002BQJ5** — Use a proper markdown renderer for detail view
  description and md viewer (completed) — the direct precedent

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `buildDescriptionPreview()`, `formatMetadataPanel()`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — description preview test suite
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts` — `renderMarkdown()` (reference, no changes)

- **WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J** — Herdr selection list: let list take as much space
  as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (the layout contract this
  change builds on: selection list keeps priority)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Performance risk**: `renderMarkdown` runs the `marked` lexer on every
  selection change. Mitigated by caching keyed on (item.id, description hash).
- **Layout shift**: Rendered markdown lines may be taller/shorter than raw
  lines; the dynamic layout already absorbs this (list keeps priority).
- **ANSI truncation risk**: Rendered output contains ANSI escape sequences;
  truncation must not break sequences mid-code (existing `truncateLine`
  handles this).
- **Scope guard**: The preview remains display-only — note-edit chords
  (WL-0MSKV6SKK008MMXR) stay in the detail view's md viewer, NOT the metadata
  panel preview.
- **Cache invalidation assumption**: Description changes only via item refresh;
  cache cleared on refresh/selection change (no filesystem watch needed).
